faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Copper-Cored Busbar suitable for Copper-cored titanium conductor busbar?
faq.a: Titanium Copper-Cored Busbar uses Grade 2 CP-Ti because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address anode system operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Copper-Cored Busbar?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Copper-Cored Busbar require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. anode system components receive Platinum cladding 2.5um minimum via electrodeposition for stable catalytic surface in electrochemical cells. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Copper-Cored Busbar shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Busbar / Conductor bar anode system components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
